name: Boris Yeltsin
summary: Yeltsin led Russia out of the Soviet Union, pushed a rapid shift to a market economy and a presidential constitution with wide executive powers, and defended Russia's territorial integrity by force in Chechnya. He dissolved parliament by decree in 1993, signed the 1997 religion law favouring Orthodoxy, and resigned early in 1999, handing power to Putin.

notes: Searched, by theme: economy (price liberalization, privatization, land), government (1993 dissolution of parliament, constitution, presidential powers), federalism (Federation Treaty, Tatarstan), society (religion law, homosexuality), liberty (death penalty), world (UN speech, NATO, Tashkent treaty, Chechnya) and means. Privatization decrees and the loans-for-shares record were looked for but the sources opened (Treisman, NBER) describe the government's program, not his own acts, so those statements stay null. Yeltsin left no memoir text in the local libraries, so many themes (race, gender, nationalism, ecology, technology, religion beyond the 1997 law) have no recorded position in the sources opened. His late regret in the 1999 farewell at having hoped for a leap to the new order in one burst is a late remark and does not change the record of the 1991-92 radical reforms; gradual-change is left null. Record over words: constitution-based answers rest on the constitution he proposed and put to referendum (CSM, 12 Nov 1993).
